questions.question: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
questions.explain: The bar has 5 equal parts and 2 are shaded, so it is 2/5. The bottom number counts all the parts, not just the white ones.

visual.caption: A bar cut into equal parts

questions.question: Mia shaded part of this bar. What fraction did she shade?
questions.explain: Count the 3 shaded parts for the top and all 8 equal parts for the bottom: 3/8. The shaded number goes on top, not on the bottom.

questions.question: Which fraction names the shaded part of this bar?
questions.explain: 7 parts are shaded out of 10 equal parts, so the fraction is 7/10. A fraction needs a top and a bottom number, not just 7.

questions.question: Which fraction shows how much of this bar is shaded?
questions.explain: 4 of the 7 equal parts are shaded, so it is 4/7. Do not use the 3 white parts as the bottom number.

visual.caption: A bar with some parts shaded

questions.question: Dad cuts a pizza into equal slices. The shaded slices have mushrooms. What fraction of the pizza has mushrooms?
questions.explain: The pizza has 8 equal slices and 5 have mushrooms, so it is 5/8. The bottom number is all the slices, not the 3 plain ones.

questions.question: A paper strip has 9 equal parts. Ava colours 4 parts blue. What fraction of the strip is blue?
questions.explain: 4 parts out of 9 equal parts are blue, so the fraction is 4/9. The blue parts go on top and all the parts go on the bottom.

questions.question: This chocolate bar has equal pieces. The shaded pieces have nuts. How do you say the fraction of the bar that has nuts?
questions.explain: 3 of the 10 equal pieces have nuts, so we say three tenths. The 7 pieces with no nuts do not name the fraction.

questions.question: A round garden is split into equal parts. The shaded parts have tulips. What fraction of the garden has tulips?
questions.explain: There are 5 equal parts and 3 have tulips, so it is 3/5. The 5 goes on the bottom because it counts the whole garden.

questions.question: A window has 9 equal panes. Finn paints 2 panes green and 5 panes yellow. What fraction of the window is painted?
questions.explain: First add the painted panes: 2 + 5 = 7. Then write 7 over all 9 panes to get 7/9, not 7 over the 2 clear panes.

questions.question: A fence has 7 equal boards. Only 2 boards are not painted. What fraction of the fence is painted?
questions.explain: First find the painted boards: 7 - 2 = 5. Then put 5 over all 7 boards, not over the 2 bare ones, to get 5/7.

questions.question: Max wrote 2/7 for the shaded part of this bar. What should Max do?
options: Write just 2, for the shaded parts.
Change the 7 to 9, all the parts.
Flip it to 9/2, with 9 on the top.
questions.explain: The bar has 9 equal parts, so the bottom number must be 9 and the fraction is 2/9. Max used the 7 white parts, but the bottom counts all the parts.

questions.question: A cake is cut into equal slices, and the shaded ones are eaten. Then Kai eats 2 more slices. What fraction of the cake is eaten now?
questions.explain: 3 slices were eaten and Kai eats 2 more, so 5 are eaten. The cake has 12 equal slices, so it is 5/12, not 5 over the 7 slices left.
